A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GARE text-video retrieval work despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GARE retrieval results on four datasets, component ablations, and analyses of embedding geometry and training dynamics.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds original ablations, gradient diagnostics, qualitative examples, update-error measurements, and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The central pair-specific increment mechanism and its Gaussian KL, norm, and directional regularizers are retained. The expanded VIB formulation and sequence-context details do not establish a changed training algorithm. Appendix I newly proposes an optional inference adaptation using ANN candidate retrieval followed by GARE reranking; it is not presented as replacing the main benchmark procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MSR-VTT, DiDeMo, ActivityNet Captions, and MSVD for the same retrieval tasks. The additional diagnostics and hard-negative examples investigate retained coverage rather than introducing another dataset, domain, or distinct input condition.

E2.justification: v5 adds numerical comparisons with T2VLA and DiCoSA on MSR-VTT, DiCoSA on DiDeMo and ActivityNet, and FROZEN on MSVD. Appendix C.5 additionally compares against DMAE and NeighborRetr, substantially expanding comparisons relevant to hard negatives. Diffusion becoming DiffusionRet is a name change, and the PDFs do not establish that the added external baselines were rerun.

E3.justification: The main backbone, retrieval metrics, batch size, and epoch budgets remain unchanged. The stated ActivityNet learning rate for non-CLIP modules changes from 3e-4 to the general 1e-4 setting, without evidence of rerunning. Added experiments introduce normalization/prior controls and efficiency measurements on four RTX 4090 GPUs. Calling the same MSR-VTT 1K-A split 'validation' instead of 'test' does not establish different samples.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining v1's regularizer and training-dynamics analyses, v5 adds gap-query versus no-gap interaction tests, Gaussian-prior and normalization ablations, additional correction/context configurations, and an orthogonality variant. New gradient diagnostics, hard-negative case studies, analytic-versus-learned update-error analysis, efficiency measurements, and candidate-coverage checks substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for retrieval results. Both use descriptive distribution means and spreads. v5's additional gradient mean/standard-deviation plots provide new diagnostic results, without establishing a changed replication or uncertainty-estimation protocol.

E6.justification: GARE's headline benchmark scores remain unchanged, including MSR-VTT text-to-video/video-to-text R@1 of 49.1/48.6. Substantial new results include no-gap interaction R@1 of 46.1 versus 49.1, prior and orthogonality comparisons, and measured computational costs. Existing norm-distribution results also change: the adjusted negative-pair mean is 13.96 in v1 Figure 2b and 12.35 in v5 Figure 3b. These changes do not establish a same-setting retrieval improvement.

T1.justification: v5 adds a formal latent-variable VIB objective, variational bounds, Jensen aggregation, and a mutual-information decomposition in Section 2.3 and Appendices D–E. Appendix H.5 adds mathematical treatment of analytic versus learned update magnitudes, and Appendix I introduces the conditional-distance argument about ANN compatibility. The main gradient equations also acquire the missing temperature factor. The original Taylor/trust-region derivation is retained and revised.

C1.justification: The central claims about pair-specific corrections relieving optimization tension and improving retrieval remain. v5 elevates relaxed VIB regularization into an explicit contribution and qualifies the abstract/conclusion's update characterization from an ideal or optimal adjustment toward locally consistent, approximate descent directions. This refines the claimed contribution without replacing the research objective.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive explanations of gradient cancellation, increment collapse, the role of bottleneck regularization, and the consequences of normalization and orthogonality. It explains the relaxed compression term as leaving text-specific conditional information unpenalized. Appendix I newly acknowledges incompatibility with direct ANN retrieval and large-scale pairwise costs. The original limitations concerning persistent modality separation and weak supervision remain.

D1.justification: v5 supplies the combined training objective and previously unspecified loss weights, including beta=0.07 and structural weights of 0.01 on MSR-VTT. It details pooled embeddings versus frame/word context sequences, module size, cached inference, and cross-attention pseudocode, and reports hardware-specific runtime, memory, and FLOPs. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is largely retained and moved to Appendix B. Added references include FROZEN, T2VLAD, DMAE, NeighborRetr, and evidential deep learning. Appendix C.5 provides a focused new positioning against hard-negative approaches, emphasizing GARE's lack of explicit mining or memory banks, rather than broadly replacing the earlier research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively revised. Related work moves to the appendix, qualitative analysis becomes part of the experiment section, and the appendices are reorganized around expanded derivations and implementation material. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v5 adds gradient plots, illustrated hard-negative examples, update-error plots, efficiency tables, and boxed inference/cross-attention pseudocode. It splits v1 Table 3 into separate tables, expands comparison tables, and redraws the norm-distribution panels with revised axes and legends. The original schematic and training-dynamics plots are retained, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the work easier to reproduce and assess through explicit loss weights, implementation and inference details, targeted ablations, measured costs, and acknowledgment of the ANN limitation. These provide a net benefit beyond the unchanged headline scores. However, new problems limit the gain: Section 3.2 claims MSVD superiority despite Table 2 showing 46.4 versus Diffusion's 46.6 R@1, and Appendix H.5 uses a parameter-space gradient as an increment update without establishing the required mapping.
